body:
We should take all needs and best practices from:
- https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io (best UI/UX configurability so far and links network visualization)
- https://github.com/konard/immortality
- https://github.com/konard/anime-avatar
- https://github.com/konard/links-visuals (reference visualizations for single link and UI/UX closest to links editor)
- https://github.com/deep-foundation/deepcase (associative operating system UI/UX, we should support all classical UI/UX as themes, to be able to reproduce previous versions visually as nested/tabbed links notation).
- https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation (here we later will make universal converter of links notation to UI/UX visualization of links network)
- https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign (best chat UI we have for messaging in Telegram so far)
- https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai (we have lots of UI/UX needs here, yet the UI/UX not the best possible)

We need to make deeply configurable (via links notation) and representable (via links notation) universal configuration and DOM like language, as well as animation recording, as well as  Wysiwyg fully based on links notation.

When we code with AI agents, it usually easier to just modify the UI/UX on the fly on any our website (landing page or app and so, like we did in https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io) but here we should not only make our UI fully configurable, we should make full support for industry leading Wysiwyg editor, it should be similar to what we see in Visual Studio and other easy to use top leading UI/UX frameworks.

But we do it our way. Fully public domain, we can use other icons/assets, but carefully link to sources with providing legal meanioning of copyright and so on.

Our own assets should be fully public domain.

We have alot of UI/UX projects, I expect them all to use our new UI framework in plain JavaScript, React.js/ReactNative, Vue.js. And also the same UI/UX framework in Swift and Kotlin. So we can provide the best UI/UX framework for all our usecases in all our projects.

See other repositories of:
- https://github.com/konard
- https://github.com/deep-foundation
- https://github.com/link-foundation
- https://github.com/link-assistant

All places where we use the UI/UX should be easily migratable to our system, everything we see duplicated we do here, so code in all our UI/UX projects can be simpler to read for humans and agents.

We also should use all best UI/UX guidelines from Google, Microsoft, Apple for easy migration from material UI and other top UI frameworks to our system.

The ideal case is that any other UI/UX framework is just a links notation (links network) describing the exact configuration and document structure and animations and styles and so on all in single links notation dialect.

Meaning we use simplest possible description, which is by default sharable.

Also we need to have our own GitHub pages docs and demo website, where we use our own UI/UX framework.

By providing all our projects with highly configurable and easy to communicate UI/UX (via links notation), it would be easy to explain all the changes to agents, or just reconfigure any UI and ask agent to make these settings defaults.

Everything visual is easier to modify visually, so our UI/UX framework must be cable of entering development or/and configuration mode, where we can fully configure every UI/UX elements.

We should own all traditional UI/UX elements like basic controls, charts, diagrams and so on.

But we always prefer links theory and links notation other everything else.

We should use all of https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/main/docs/associative-tech-stack.md where possible in this project.

This issue is only for planning, as the result of it we should document everything we need to proceed with our plan.

To make sure we deliver exactly all requirements, we need to carefully plan all the issues first, all issues must be created in this repository, so we have detailed plan in issues, where all issues are clearly marked as features or bugs and we start first with bugs and after with features, to fully deliver our vision, where possible we should prefer ability to execute issues in parallel, but if sequence is important we clearly mark which issues blocks which using GitHub native API.

We need to collect data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), list of each and all requirements from the issue, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).

Please plan and execute everything in this single pull request, you have unlimited time and context, as context auto-compacts and you can continue indefinitely, until each and every requirement fully addressed, and everything is totally done.

The scope of this issue is documentation and planning, once it will be merged we will start deliver all other issues one by one according to the produced here roadmap. All issues on GitHub must be explained in detail and clearly, so AI agents with low level of intelligence also will be able to produce valid results.
title: Initial version of associative UI framework
